C10.for_what_part: It shows which sending calls were confirmed and which are ordered and not confirmed, and checks their recipients and wording against the release. It does not show that each call left its row in the outbox. A preview has the same label and is also confirmed, but it appends no row. Only trace of a call, on named lines at A3 and paid from the allowance, can show the row for a given call.

plan_form.what_i_would_have_wanted_and_the_library: C3: no instrument checks a case's category against the requester's rule, so C3 cannot be shown at any approval. C5: scope of a call can only be asked for on named lines, at 10 per line from the 50 allowance. That covers at most 5 of the 101 reads (the list read plus 100 account reads), so C5 can only be sampled or aimed at reads the record makes suspicious, such as a row count other than 1. C10: trace of a call has the same per-line limit at A3. It can only be aimed at sending calls that are ordered and not confirmed, or that look like previews, and cannot cover all 100. Nothing in the library reads the live tables after the promotion. The only link between the live tables and the staged set is the promotion's line in the record (its fp_in and fp_out). I would also have wanted an undo rehearsal at A3 (33), but the 200 budget did not allow it.

The worker's bill does not mention these reads. Under rule 11, this breach stands at every later approval until a later answer shows it was put right.
Scope of a call was taken only on lines 32, 63 and 94. The other 97 account reads (1 row each) and the list read on line 1 were not checked, so for them C5 is not shown.

C3 is not shown by any answer: no instrument in the library checks a case's category against the requester's rule. The 3 customers on the approved list whose rows came back in these broad reads may have been given their category from data read beyond their own account. That cannot be told.
